entries.answer: Humanpower is the productive capability of a human network: the range of action available to its people, the quality of their decisions, and the speed and integrity with which they coordinate. We measure a baseline across range of action, decision quality, coordination latency, context retention, trust and agency, and learning rate. There is no single humanpower score; the receipt is a before-and-after account of what changed, for whom, at what cost, and with which risks.
entries.label: Humanpower

entries.answer: Idea Nexus Ventures builds and studies systems that increase the productive power of human networks. We work in three connected ways: HumAIn products, organizational AI transformation, and market intelligence.
entries.label: Shared principles

entries.answer: The AI audit is a paid organizational integration diagnostic. It maps real workflows, priorities, constraints, governance boundaries, and AI fit, then recommends the smallest credible intervention. The answer may be no AI, process redesign, conventional automation, or a bounded HumAIn pilot.
entries.label: The AI audit

entries.answer: HumAIn products connect AI to people, decisions, relationships, workflows, and institutional memory. The test is whether the system increases human agency and coordination without hiding provenance or uncertainty.
entries.label: HumAIn products

entries.answer: Organizational transformation starts with how work actually happens. We identify where AI can create leverage, where process redesign is required first, and what small pilot can prove the difference.
entries.label: Organizational transformation

entries.answer: Market intelligence at Idea Nexus uses network, trust, and information lenses. A useful thesis states its mechanism, evidence, leading indicators, and what would falsify it.
entries.label: Market intelligence

entries.answer: The shared method is: observe the network, preserve the provenance, find the leverage, run the smallest credible test, and measure what changed. We do not assume AI is the answer.
entries.label: Shared principles

entries.answer: AI is the wrong intervention when the bottleneck is unclear ownership, broken process, missing data, insufficient authority, or a problem that conventional software solves more simply. A credible audit must be allowed to recommend against AI.
entries.label: When not to use AI
